```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# The guide lives two levels below the repository root; every path
# below is written from the root, as the exercises are.
repo_root <- normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), '..', '..'))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_root)
pkgload::load_all(repo_root, quiet = TRUE)
extract_path <- file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'data', 'raw_data',
                          'cohort_raw.csv')
if (!file.exists(extract_path)) {
  stop('The cohort extract is missing. Run ',
       'Rscript analysis/scripts/simulate_cohort.R ',
       'from the repository root, then render again.')
}
code <- function(x) paste0('\x60', x, '\x60')
dq <- function(x) code(paste0('"', x, '"'))
pa <- function(x) if (isTRUE(x)) 'present' else 'absent'
words <- function(x) knitr::combine_words(x, before = '\x60')
```

```{r}
#| label: repo-state
#| include: false
git_out <- function(...) {
  out <- suppressWarnings(system2('git', c('-C', repo_root, ...),
                                  stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE))
  if (is.null(attr(out, 'status'))) out else character(0)
}
git_head <- git_out('rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD')
git_dirty <- length(git_out('status', '--porcelain')) > 0
has_lock <- file.exists(file.path(repo_root, 'renv.lock'))
has_docker <- file.exists(file.path(repo_root, 'Dockerfile'))
rung <- if (has_lock && has_docker) {
  'L2'
} else if (has_lock) {
  'L1'
} else {
  'L0'
}
rung_name <- c(
  L0 = 'locatable', L1 = 'pinned packages',
  L2 = 'pinned environment'
)[[rung]]
next_artifact <- c(
  L0 = 'a lockfile, `renv.lock`',
  L1 = 'a container recipe, a `Dockerfile`',
  L2 = 'a baseline test that passes after a clean rebuild'
)[[rung]]
gen_lines <- readLines(
  file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'scripts', 'simulate_cohort.R'))
gen_seed <- trimws(grep('^set\\.seed\\(', gen_lines, value = TRUE))
gen_sets_kind <- any(grepl('RNGkind', gen_lines))
stopifnot(length(gen_seed) == 1)
```

This guide is for course instructors and is distributed
separately from the book. It holds the grading key for
Exercise 7 of each of Chapters 2 to 13, the cohort-based
exercise that a script can grade, and a grading note for
the paired-review Exercise 9 of Chapter 11. It also holds
the course material: a week-by-week plan of the
one-quarter core path, a schedule of low-stakes cumulative
quizzes, notes on grading, and the rough edges we know of.
Solutions for every other exercise, and the answers to the
checks, appear in the book itself.

Exercise 7 in every chapter asks the student to apply the
chapter's core tool or concept to the running cohort
compendium (`analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv`,
generated by `analysis/scripts/simulate_cohort.R`). For
each chapter we give the key as the output of executed
code, a brief interpretation rubric, and the common errors
the instructor should watch for. Nothing in a key is typed:
every value below was computed when this guide was
rendered, on commit `r git_head` of the repository
`r if (git_dirty) 'with uncommitted changes in the working tree' else 'with a clean working tree'`.
Render the guide again after the repository changes, and
the keys follow.

The generator calls `r code(gen_seed)` and is
deterministic, so the values are exact for a given
extract. The generator
`r if (gen_sets_kind) 'fixes the random-number kind itself' else 'does not call RNGkind(), so it uses the R release\'s default sampler'`.
A student whose values differ therefore has an edited
generator, an edited extract, a different version of
`clean_cohort()` than the one shipped with the book, or a
session that overrides the default sampler. Each of these
deviations is diagnostically useful and merits discussion.

# Exercise 7 keys {#sec-ig-keys}

## Chapter 2: The Reproducibility Crisis {#sec-ig-ch01}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch01
raw <- load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
class(raw$sex)

legacy <- utils::read.csv(
  'analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv',
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
class(legacy$sex)
```

**Autogradable values:** `class(raw$sex)` =
`r dq(class(raw$sex))`; `class(legacy$sex)` =
`r dq(class(legacy$sex))`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer names the two class strings and
explains that the difference demonstrates the R-runtime
layer. `stringsAsFactors` is an R default, not a package
default or a property of the data, and its value flipped
between R releases. `load_cohort()` closes the exposure at
the analysis-code layer by stating the choice explicitly.

**Common errors.** Confusing the R-runtime layer with the
package-versions layer; omitting the explanation of which
determinant-stack layer the difference occupies.

## Chapter 3: Levels of Reproducibility {#sec-ig-ch02}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch02
cohort <- clean_cohort(
  load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv'))
nrow(cohort)

# Recomputed by the code of the unlabeled `repo_state` chunk in
# analysis/report/02-levels-of-reproducibility.qmd ('The cohort,
# continued'), with paths written from the repository root.
repo_state <- c(
  source_code = file.exists('R/cohort.R'),
  data_generator = file.exists('analysis/scripts/simulate_cohort.R'),
  lockfile = file.exists('renv.lock'),
  dockerfile = file.exists('Dockerfile')
)
repo_state
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch02-lock
#| include: false
locked <- names(renv::lockfile_read('renv.lock')$Packages)
tibble_locked <- 'tibble' %in% locked
```

**Autogradable value:** `nrow(cohort)` = `r nrow(cohort)`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports `r nrow(cohort)` rows
and places the compendium from the `file.exists()` checks
the exercise asks for. On the repository when this guide
was rendered, `renv.lock` is
`r pa(repo_state[['lockfile']])` and `Dockerfile` is
`r pa(repo_state[['dockerfile']])`, so the compendium is at
`r rung` (`r rung_name`), and the artifact missing for the
next rung is `r next_artifact`. The chapter's `repo_state`
chunk computes the same values at render time. The
lockfile `r if (tibble_locked) 'records' else 'does not record'`
`tibble`, and records every other non-base package it
pins; base packages such as `stats` and `utils` have no
record.

**Common errors.** Claiming L1 because the code is under
version control (version control is L0); confusing 'pinned'
with 'committed'; reporting a rung from memory rather than
from the checks.

## Chapter 4: Version Control with Git and GitHub {#sec-ig-vc}

```{r}
#| label: ig-vc
raw <- load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
nrow(raw)
intersect(c('mrn', 'patient_name', 'dob'), names(raw))
```

```{bash}
#| label: ig-vc-git
git check-ignore -v analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv
git log --all --oneline -- inst/testdata/cohort_raw.csv
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-vc-history
#| include: false
id_cols <- intersect(c('mrn', 'patient_name', 'dob'), names(raw))
ignore_hit <- git_out('check-ignore', '-v',
                      'analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
ignore_source <- sub('\t.*$', '', ignore_hit)
ignore_pattern <- sub('^[^:]*:[0-9]+:', '', ignore_source)
stopifnot(length(ignore_pattern) == 1)

# Recomputed by the code of the unlabeled chunk that defines
# `old_copy_has_identifiers` in analysis/report/version-control.qmd
# (the `.gitignore` section), with `-C` pointing at the repository
# root.
fixture_path <- 'inst/testdata/cohort_raw.csv'
fixture_log <- git_out('log', '--all', '--format=%h', '--',
                       fixture_path)
oldest_copy <- utils::tail(fixture_log, 1)
oldest_header <- if (length(oldest_copy) == 1) {
  utils::head(git_out('show',
                      paste0(oldest_copy, ':', fixture_path)), 1)
} else {
  character(0)
}
old_copy_has_identifiers <- length(oldest_header) == 1 &&
  all(c('patient_name', 'dob') %in%
        strsplit(gsub('"', '', oldest_header), ',')[[1]])
current_header <- names(utils::read.csv(fixture_path, nrows = 1))
current_has_identifiers <- any(c('patient_name', 'dob') %in%
                                 current_header)
```

**Autogradable values:** `nrow(raw)` = `r nrow(raw)`;
`r length(id_cols)` of the three identifier columns present
(`r words(id_cols)`); the excluding line is
`r code(ignore_source)`, the directory pattern
`r code(ignore_pattern)` (the line number moves if
`.gitignore` is edited).

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports `r nrow(raw)` rows (the
raw extract before cleaning, including the planted
duplicate), names all three identifier-shaped columns, and
identifies the directory pattern, not a single filename, as
what excludes the extract. For the `git log` step it
explains what the oldest commit listed holds. On this
render the log lists `r length(fixture_log)`
`r if (length(fixture_log) == 1) 'commit' else 'commits'`,
and the oldest, `r code(oldest_copy)`,
`r if (old_copy_has_identifiers) 'holds an earlier copy of the extract whose header names patient_name and dob' else 'holds no copy with the identifier columns'`.
`r if (old_copy_has_identifiers) 'The ignore pattern protected one path, and the same bytes entered the history through a second path.' else 'If the history has been rewritten since the chapter was written, the chapter\'s own render shows the same result.'`
The current fixture at that path
`r if (current_has_identifiers) 'still carries identifier columns' else 'carries no name or date-of-birth column'`,
but an old copy remains in the history until the history is
rewritten.

**Common errors.** Using `nrow(cohort)`
(`r nrow(clean_cohort(raw))`) instead of `nrow(raw)`
(`r nrow(raw)`); concluding from `git check-ignore` alone
that the identifier columns never entered the history.

## Chapter 5: The Research Compendium {#sec-ig-ch03}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch03
raw <- load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
cohort <- clean_cohort(raw)
nrow(raw)
nrow(cohort)

# Recomputed by the code of the unlabeled `pillars` chunk in
# analysis/report/03-research-compendium.qmd ('The cohort,
# continued'), with paths written from the repository root.
pillars <- c(
  environment_dockerfile = file.exists('Dockerfile'),
  packages_renv_lock = file.exists('renv.lock'),
  session_rprofile = file.exists('.Rprofile'),
  source_code_r_cohort = file.exists('R/cohort.R'),
  data_generator = file.exists('analysis/scripts/simulate_cohort.R')
)
pillars
sum(pillars)
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch03-text
#| include: false
pillar_label <- c(
  environment_dockerfile = 'the environment pillar (`Dockerfile`)',
  packages_renv_lock = 'the package-versions pillar (`renv.lock`)',
  session_rprofile = 'the session pillar (`.Rprofile`)',
  source_code_r_cohort = 'the source-code pillar (`R/cohort.R`)',
  data_generator = 'the data pillar (`simulate_cohort.R`)'
)
pillars_absent <- if (any(!pillars)) {
  paste(pillar_label[!pillars], collapse = ' and ')
} else {
  'no pillar'
}
```

**Autogradable values:** `nrow(raw)` = `r nrow(raw)`;
`nrow(cohort)` = `r nrow(cohort)`; `sum(pillars)` =
`r sum(pillars)` of five.

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports the three numbers,
names what is missing (on this render,
`r pillars_absent`), and places the compendium at
`r rung`. The rung is set by which pillar is missing, not
by how many are present: L1 requires the lockfile and L2
requires an environment recipe as well, so
`r sum(pillars)` of five pillars with
`r if (pillars[['environment_dockerfile']]) 'the recipe present' else 'the recipe absent'`
is `r rung`, not a fraction of the way to the next rung.

**Common errors.** Placing the compendium at a higher rung,
or 'between rungs', on the pillar count; checking the
gitignored CSV rather than the committed generator.

## Chapter 6: Pinning Packages with renv {#sec-ig-ch04}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch04
deps <- renv::dependencies(
  c('R/cohort.R', 'analysis/scripts/simulate_cohort.R'),
  quiet = TRUE
)
unique(deps$Package)
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch04-count
#| include: false
# The counting rule of the `tbl-cohort-deps` chunk in
# analysis/report/04-dependencies.qmd.
found_pkgs <- sort(unique(deps$Package))
base_pkgs <- rownames(installed.packages(priority = 'base'))
found_base <- intersect(found_pkgs, base_pkgs)
contributed <- setdiff(found_pkgs, base_pkgs)
unpinned <- setdiff(contributed, locked)
sim_rows <- sum(basename(deps$Source) == 'simulate_cohort.R')
```

**Autogradable values:** `r length(found_pkgs)` referenced
packages; contributed (non-base) packages =
`r words(contributed)`, so the count is
`r length(contributed)`. The chapter's `tbl-cohort-deps`
chunk computes both at render time.

**Rubric.** A correct answer applies the chapter's counting
rule: base packages are those `installed.packages(priority =
'base')` lists (here `r words(found_base)`), and
recommended packages such as `survival` count, because
`renv` records them. It notes that
`r if (length(unpinned) == 0) 'every contributed package is' else paste('the scan finds', words(unpinned), 'not')`
pinned in the committed lockfile. `simulate_cohort.R`
contributes `r sim_rows` rows because it has no `library()`
or `pkg::` reference.

**Common errors.** Excluding `survival` as a recommended
package; listing base packages as needing lockfile entries;
not checking the generator script separately.

## Chapter 7: Pinning the Environment with Docker {#sec-ig-ch05}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch05
raw <- load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
cohort <- clean_cohort(raw)
nrow(cohort)
length(unique(cohort$sex))
file.exists('Dockerfile')
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch05-text
#| include: false
# The lockfile's R version, as the `cohort-lockfile-r` chunk of
# analysis/report/05-containers.qmd reads it.
lock_r <- jsonlite::read_json('renv.lock')$R$Version
# The thread variables of the showcase Dockerfile: the first
# ```docker block of the chapter that has both a digest-pinned FROM
# line and an ENV instruction, so that the key follows the text.
ch7 <- readLines('analysis/report/05-containers.qmd')
openers <- grep('^```docker\\s*$', ch7)
closers <- grep('^```\\s*$', ch7)
blocks <- lapply(openers, function(o) ch7[o:min(closers[closers > o])])
is_showcase <- vapply(blocks, function(b) {
  any(grepl('^FROM rocker/r-ver:[^ ]+@sha256:', b)) &&
    any(grepl('^ENV ', b))
}, logical(1))
stopifnot(any(is_showcase))
showcase <- blocks[[which(is_showcase)[1]]]
thread_vars <- unique(regmatches(
  showcase, regexpr('[A-Z]+_NUM_THREADS=[0-9]+', showcase)))
stopifnot(length(thread_vars) >= 1)
```

**Autogradable values:** `nrow(cohort)` = `r nrow(cohort)`;
`length(unique(cohort$sex))` = `r length(unique(cohort$sex))`;
`file.exists('Dockerfile')` = `r file.exists('Dockerfile')`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports all three values. The
`Dockerfile` is `r pa(has_docker)`, so the compendium is at
`r rung`, with the lockfile recording R `r lock_r`; a recipe
for L2 starts from `r code(paste0('rocker/r-ver:', lock_r))`,
matching the lockfile's R. The `ENV` instruction of the
chapter's showcase Dockerfile pins the thread count with
`r words(thread_vars)`.

**Common errors.** Reporting `unique(cohort$sex)` (the
strings) rather than `length(unique(cohort$sex))` (the
integer); naming only `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, when the showcase
`ENV` instruction also sets the OpenBLAS variable, because
the Rocker image links R against OpenBLAS, which reads its
own variable.

## Chapter 8: Backends and Runtimes {#sec-ig-ch06}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch06
# The artifact check of 'The cohort, continued' in
# analysis/report/06-backends-runtimes.qmd, run from the root.
repo_root_rel <- '.'
backend_artifacts <- c(
  renv.lock = file.exists(file.path(repo_root_rel, 'renv.lock')),
  Dockerfile = file.exists(file.path(repo_root_rel, 'Dockerfile')),
  default.nix = file.exists(file.path(repo_root_rel, 'default.nix')),
  devcontainer = file.exists(
    file.path(repo_root_rel, '.devcontainer', 'devcontainer.json')))
backend_artifacts
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch06-text
#| include: false
dev_path <- file.path('.devcontainer', 'devcontainer.json')
dev_image <- if (file.exists(dev_path)) {
  hit <- grep('"image"\\s*:', readLines(dev_path), value = TRUE)
  sub('.*"image"\\s*:\\s*"([^"]+)".*', '\\1', hit[1])
} else {
  NA_character_
}
```

**Expected result:**
`r paste(backend_artifacts, collapse = ', ')`, in the order
`renv.lock`, `Dockerfile`, `default.nix`, `devcontainer`.
The chapter's artifact-check chunk prints the same values
at render time.

**Rubric.** A qualitative answer is expected here. A correct
answer places the compendium at `r rung` and identifies Nix
via `rix` (axis two) as the backend that could lift it to
L2 without a Docker image. Axis one needs an image to swap
the runtime on, and
`r if (has_docker) 'the Dockerfile now defines one' else 'there is none yet'`.
`r if (backend_artifacts[['devcontainer']] && !is.na(dev_image)) paste0('Axis three\'s only existing artifact, the devcontainer, starts from the generic image ', code(dev_image), ' rather than from a compendium-specific one.') else 'No development container is in place.'`

**Common errors.** Treating the devcontainer as evidence of
L2 (it points at a generic image, not a compendium-specific
one); not explaining why axis two is the available path.

## Chapter 9: Literate Programming and the Rendered Report {#sec-ig-ch07}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch07
cohort <- clean_cohort(
  load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv'))
n_cohort <- nrow(cohort)
pct_missing <- round(100 * mean(is.na(cohort$incident_dm)), 1)
n_cohort
pct_missing
```

**Autogradable values:** `n_cohort` = `r n_cohort`;
`pct_missing` = `r pct_missing`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer inserts both values as inline R
expressions (`r knitr::inline_expr('n_cohort')` and
`r knitr::inline_expr('pct_missing')`) rather than typing
them after a console check. The sealed sentence reads: 'The
cleaned cohort holds `r n_cohort` records, of which
`r pct_missing` percent carry no recorded outcome.'

**Common errors.** Typing the numbers directly in prose
rather than using inline expressions; using `nrow(raw)`
(`r nrow(raw)`) instead of `nrow(cohort)` (`r n_cohort`).

## Chapter 10: Automating the Analysis: Make and targets {#sec-ig-pipelines}

```{r}
#| label: ig-pipelines
cohort <- clean_cohort(
  load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv'))
nrow(cohort)
```

**Autogradable value:** `nrow(cohort)` = `r nrow(cohort)`.

**`_targets.R` fragment** (display only; this guide does not
run `targets`):

```{.r}
list(
  tar_target(
    raw_file,
    'analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv',
    format = 'file'
  ),
  tar_target(raw, load_cohort(raw_file)),
  tar_target(cleaned, clean_cohort(raw))
)
```

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports `r nrow(cohort)` rows
and includes a `_targets.R` fragment with a
`format = 'file'` target for the CSV. Immediately after the
first `tar_make()`, and again after a second run with no
file changed, `tar_outdated()` should return an empty
result, because all three targets (`raw_file`, `raw`,
`cleaned`) are up to date. This expectation follows from
`targets` semantics; the guide does not execute it.

**Common errors.** Omitting the `format = 'file'` target
for the CSV (meaning file-content changes would not
re-trigger downstream targets). Placing the compendium at
L3 because the pipeline runs green: a pipeline pins no
determinant, so the compendium stays at the rung its
capture artifacts set, `r rung` on this render.

## Chapter 11: Testing and Code Quality {#sec-ig-ch08}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch08
raw <- load_cohort('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
cohort <- clean_cohort(raw)

checks <- list(
  columns = tinytest::expect_true(
    all(c('mrn', 'age_at_enroll', 'sex', 'incident_dm') %in%
          names(raw))),
  age_range = tinytest::expect_true(
    all(cohort$age_at_enroll >= 18 &
          cohort$age_at_enroll <= 105, na.rm = TRUE)),
  sex_coding = tinytest::expect_true(
    all(cohort$sex %in% c('F', 'M'))),
  missing_outcome = tinytest::expect_true(
    mean(is.na(cohort$incident_dm)) < 0.15)
)
vapply(checks, isTRUE, logical(1))

nrow(raw)
nrow(cohort)
sum(duplicated(raw$mrn))
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch08-check
#| include: false
n_dup <- sum(duplicated(raw$mrn))
stopifnot(nrow(raw) - nrow(cohort) == n_dup)
```

**Autogradable values:** `nrow(raw)` = `r nrow(raw)`;
`nrow(cohort)` = `r nrow(cohort)`;
`sum(duplicated(raw$mrn))` = `r n_dup`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports all three counts,
identifies the `r n_dup` duplicate
`r if (n_dup == 1) 'row' else 'rows'` removed by
`clean_cohort()`, and shows four passing `expect_true()`
assertions covering required columns, age range, sex coding,
and missing-outcome rate. Against the extract on this
render, `r sum(vapply(checks, isTRUE, logical(1)))` of the
four assertions pass.

**Common errors.** Reporting `nrow(cohort)` =
`r nrow(raw)` (forgetting that `clean_cohort()` removes
duplicates); writing assertions that pass trivially (for
example, `expect_true(TRUE)`).

**Exercise 9 (paired review).** Graded on the review record,
not on a number: at least one comment for each of the six
checklist questions that applies, replies from the author, an
`all.equal()` comparison of the two outputs after sorting by
`mrn`, and one discrepancy attributed to review and one to the
comparison (or a reasoned 'none'). Findings to expect include
age rows dropped rather than set to missing, missing-outcome
rows dropped in cleaning, and an unstated rule for which
duplicate to keep.

## Chapter 12: Continuous Integration and Verification {#sec-ig-ch09}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch09
# The lines of the `ci-ex7-key` chunk in
# analysis/report/09-continuous-integration.qmd, run from the root.
script <- 'R/cohort.R'
locked_real <- names(renv::lockfile_read('renv.lock')$Packages)
base_pkgs <- rownames(installed.packages(priority = 'base'))
used <- unique(renv::dependencies(script, quiet = TRUE)$Package)
missing <- setdiff(used, c(locked_real, base_pkgs))
length(missing)
n_missing_real <- length(missing)

script <- file.path(tempdir(), 'cohort_copy.R')
invisible(file.copy('R/cohort.R', script, overwrite = TRUE))
cat('library(sandwich)\n', file = script, append = TRUE)
used <- unique(renv::dependencies(script, quiet = TRUE)$Package)
missing <- setdiff(used, c(locked_real, base_pkgs))
missing
```

**Autogradable values:** `length(missing)` =
`r n_missing_real` against the real `R/cohort.R`; after
appending `library(sandwich)` and re-running the same lines,
`missing` = `r if (length(missing) == 0) 'character(0)' else paste(vapply(missing, dq, character(1)), collapse = ', ')`.

**Rubric.** A correct answer reports `r n_missing_real`
undeclared packages against the real `R/cohort.R`, and
`r words(missing)` as what the synthetic addition leaves
undeclared. The exercise demonstrates that a
dependency-manifest gate can catch an undeclared import
before CI runs a render.

**Common errors.** Running `renv::dependencies()` on the
whole project rather than on `R/cohort.R` alone; not
testing the planted `library(sandwich)` scenario.

## Chapter 13: Collaboration, Archiving, and Stewardship {#sec-ig-ch10}

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch10
# The checks of the `cohort-deposit-checks` chunk in
# analysis/report/10-archiving-sharing.qmd, with `repo <- '.'`
# as the exercise asks.
repo <- '.'
in_repo <- function(path) file.exists(file.path(repo, path))
git_ignores <- function(path) {
  if (!nzchar(Sys.which('git'))) return(NA)
  status <- system2(
    'git',
    c('-C', repo, 'check-ignore', '--no-index', '--quiet', path),
    stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE
  )
  if (status %in% c(0L, 1L)) status == 0L else NA
}
deposit <- c(
  LICENSE = in_repo('LICENSE'),
  DESCRIPTION = in_repo('DESCRIPTION'),
  renv.lock = in_repo('renv.lock'),
  Dockerfile = in_repo('Dockerfile'),
  .dockerignore = in_repo('.dockerignore'),
  cohort_csv_ignored =
    git_ignores('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv'),
  second_file_ignored =
    git_ignores('analysis/data/raw_data/my_extract.csv'))
deposit
```

```{bash}
#| label: ig-ch10-git
git check-ignore --no-index -v analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv
git check-ignore --no-index -v analysis/data/raw_data/my_extract.csv
```

```{r}
#| label: ig-ch10-text
#| include: false
rule_of <- function(path) {
  hit <- git_out('check-ignore', '--no-index', '-v', path)
  sub('^[^:]*:[0-9]+:', '', sub('\t.*$', '', hit))
}
rule_cohort <- rule_of('analysis/data/raw_data/cohort_raw.csv')
rule_second <- rule_of('analysis/data/raw_data/my_extract.csv')
same_rule <- length(rule_cohort) == 1 &&
  identical(rule_cohort, rule_second)
present_names <- names(deposit)[1:5][deposit[1:5]]
absent_names <- names(deposit)[1:5][!deposit[1:5]]
```

**Autogradable values:** on this render the chunk reports
`r words(present_names)` present and
`r if (length(absent_names) == 0) 'nothing' else words(absent_names)`
absent; both the extract and the invented second filename
`r if (all(deposit[6:7])) 'are' else 'are not both'` ignored.
`r if (same_rule) paste0('Both commands name the same directory pattern, ', code(rule_cohort), '.') else 'The two commands do not name the same rule; inspect .gitignore before grading.'`
A student's invented filename will differ from
`my_extract.csv`; the rule reported should not.

**Rubric.** A correct answer shows that the invented
filename is ignored, and explains why that is the check that
matters: a rule naming one file protects only that file,
while the directory pattern protects any extract saved
there, and a text search of `.gitignore` cannot tell the two
apart. It then names at least one check that must still
change or be added before real data. A `.dockerignore` that
excludes the data directory must exist before any
`Dockerfile` copies the project into an image, and the
deposit itself changes (a data-availability statement and a
synthetic stand-in in place of the extract).

**Common errors.** Testing only the existing filename;
stating that no check needs to change for real data;
confusing the file-system audit with the deposit decision.

# Teaching the course {#sec-ig-course}

## The one-quarter core path, by week {#sec-ig-weeks}

The book's Conventions page marks each chapter Core or
Optional for a ten-week quarter. The table below follows it
in the book's chapter order, with a week number, a graded
lab on the cohort compendium, and a link to the chapter's
Exercise 7 key in this guide.

| Week | Chapters | Graded lab, on the cohort compendium | Key |
|---|------------------|--------------------|-----|
| 1 | Preface; Ch 1, Introduction: reproducibility as a computational problem; Ch 2, The Reproducibility Crisis | Setup check; the RNG-kind comparison (Exercise 3) | [Ch 2](#sec-ig-ch01) |
| 2 | Ch 3, Levels of Reproducibility | Place a published paper on the ladder (Exercise 2), graded against a rubric, not a single answer | [Ch 3](#sec-ig-ch02) |
| 3 | Ch 4, Version Control with Git and GitHub | A course repository with `.gitignore` written before the synthetic extract is added | [Ch 4](#sec-ig-vc) |
| 4 | Ch 5, The Research Compendium | Convert a scatter of scripts into a compendium; add a README and data dictionary | [Ch 5](#sec-ig-ch03) |
| 5 | Ch 6, Pinning Packages with renv | A lockfile, then a restore on a second machine | [Ch 6](#sec-ig-ch04) |
| 6 | Ch 7, Pinning the Environment with Docker | A digest-pinned image, built locally with `--platform linux/amd64` and its digest recorded | [Ch 7](#sec-ig-ch05) |
| 7 | Ch 9, Literate Programming and the Rendered Report; the Make section of Ch 10, Automating the Analysis: Make and targets | A sealed render with every number computed inline | [Ch 9](#sec-ig-ch07), [Ch 10](#sec-ig-pipelines) |
| 8 | Ch 11, Testing and Code Quality | Data-validation tests for the extract's planted defects (Exercise 7); an oracle test and a baseline test | [Ch 11](#sec-ig-ch08) |
| 9 | Ch 12, Continuous Integration and Verification | A CI workflow that compares to a committed baseline, demonstrated failing once on purpose | [Ch 12](#sec-ig-ch09) |
| 10 | Ch 13, Collaboration, Archiving, and Stewardship | Deposit to the Zenodo sandbox; rewrite the data-availability statement for a registry extract held under a data-use agreement (Exercise 4) | [Ch 13](#sec-ig-ch10) |

```{r}
#| label: ig-weeks-check
#| include: false
# Fail the render if a chapter named in the week table has been
# renamed in the book, so that the table cannot drift silently.
book_files <- list.files('analysis/report', pattern = '\\.qmd$',
                         full.names = TRUE)
h1 <- unlist(lapply(book_files, function(f) {
  first <- grep('^# ', readLines(f, warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)[1]
  trimws(sub('\\{.*\\}', '', sub('^# ', '', first)))
}))
table_titles <- c(
  'Introduction: reproducibility as a computational problem',
  'The Reproducibility Crisis', 'Levels of Reproducibility',
  'Version Control with Git and GitHub', 'The Research Compendium',
  'Pinning Packages with renv', 'Pinning the Environment with Docker',
  'Backends and Runtimes: Nix, Podman, and Apptainer',
  'Literate Programming and the Rendered Report',
  'Automating the Analysis: Make and targets',
  'Testing and Code Quality',

stopifnot(all(table_titles %in% h1))
```

Chapter 8, Backends and Runtimes: Nix, Podman, and
Apptainer, and the `targets`, Snakemake, Nextflow, and
workflowr material of Chapter 10 are optional at this pace.
A two-quarter offering can restore them in a second term.

## Low-stakes cumulative quizzes {#sec-ig-quizzes}

```{r}
#| label: ig-quiz-chapters
#| include: false
chapter_files <- c(
  '01-reproducibility-crisis.qmd', '02-levels-of-reproducibility.qmd',
  'version-control.qmd', '03-research-compendium.qmd',
  '04-dependencies.qmd', '05-containers.qmd',
  '06-backends-runtimes.qmd', '07-literate-programming.qmd',
  'pipelines.qmd', '08-testing-quality.qmd',
  '09-continuous-integration.qmd', '10-archiving-sharing.qmd')
chapter_numbers <- 2:13
has_cumulative <- vapply(chapter_files, function(f) {
  any(grepl('^## Check your understanding: from earlier chapters',
            readLines(file.path('analysis/report', f), warn = FALSE)))
}, logical(1))
ch_label <- function(n) {
  if (length(n) == 0) character(0) else paste0('Ch ', n)
}
with_check <- ch_label(chapter_numbers[has_cumulative])
without_check <- ch_label(chapter_numbers[!has_cumulative])
```

Most checks in the book test the section just read. That
is comprehension practice, and it gives none of the benefit
of spacing: the gap between study and retrieval that helps
retention grows with how long the material must be kept
(Cepeda et al., 2006), and in a quarter-long course with a
final project that gap is weeks. Interleaving helps most
when the categories to be told apart are confusable
(Brunmair and Richter, 2019). The course's central skill,
diagnosing which determinant layer failed, is such a set.

The book now opens chapters with a folded check titled
'Check your understanding: from earlier chapters', a short
retrieval question drawn from two or more earlier
chapters. When this guide was rendered, the chapters
carrying one were
`r if (length(with_check) == 0) 'none' else knitr::combine_words(with_check)`
`r if (length(without_check) == 0) '(all of them)' else paste0('(not yet ', knitr::combine_words(without_check), ')')`.
We suggest building a short quiz on them.

- **When.** The first ten minutes of each class meeting
  from week 2 on, before the week's new material, closed
  book.
- **What.** Three to five items. One is a variant of the
  'from earlier chapters' check of the chapter being
  started, with the vignette's details changed so that the
  folded answer cannot simply be recalled. One or two
  return to material at least two weeks old. One is a
  diagnosis vignette: a failed re-run, for which the
  student names the determinant layer that changed
  (package versions, operating system and system
  libraries, R runtime and its default sampler, a stale
  derived file, the raw data, or the analysis code) and the
  earlier tool or rung that would have caught or prevented
  it.
- **Stakes.** Completion credit, or a small share of the
  grade with the lowest few dropped. The purpose is
  retrieval, not ranking; review the answers in class at
  once.
- **Week 9.** A longer mixed set of ten or so diagnosis
  vignettes across all layers, as preparation for the
  verification lab, since a CI failure log is exactly such
  a diagnosis.
- **Week 10.** A cumulative quiz that revisits one item
  from every earlier week.

When writing items, hold to the book's ladder rules as it
now states them. No rung guarantees the numerical
libraries (BLAS, LAPACK). The R release fixes the default
sampler at L2, but an `RNGkind()` override is fixed only by
an explicit call in the analysis code. A Dockerfile without
a lockfile is L0, because the rungs are cumulative.

## On grading {#sec-ig-grading}

```{r}
#| label: ig-exercise-count
#| include: false
n_exercises <- sum(vapply(chapter_files, function(f) {
  sum(grepl('^## Exercise [0-9]+\\s*$',
            readLines(file.path('analysis/report', f), warn = FALSE)))
}, integer(1)))
```

Most of the book's `r n_exercises` exercises in Chapters 2
to 13 are retrieval practice or short arguments, and their
printed solutions serve that purpose well: a student checks
their own reasoning against a worked answer. They were not
designed to be collected for a grade, and collecting them
as written has two problems. First, several ask the student
to work from their own paper, analysis, or data, which
cannot be graded consistently and, for an extract that might
carry patient information, is itself a data-governance risk
the book argues against. Second, every solution other than
Exercise 7's is printed, so a submitted answer cannot be
distinguished from a copied one.

The ten weekly labs above are designed instead: each works
the shared cohort compendium, each has a checkable output
(a restored lockfile, a CI run that is red and then green, a
rendered document with a specific inline number), and none
depends on a student's own data. `REFACTOR-PLAN.md` phase 10
(G, running study) plans a template repository, built from
the same compendium with its planted defects, distributed
through GitHub Classroom or GitLab, and autograded by CI;
until that repository exists, the labs above can be run by
hand against the same checklist.

The autograder depends on two fixes made to the `zzcollab`
and `zzrenvcheck` tools in Phase 6: `make docker-test` exits
nonzero when a test fails, and `zzc verify --full` requires
a baseline test before it stamps a compendium L3. A course
built on an unpatched install of either tool will accept a
failing submission as passing.

## Known rough edges, by week {#sec-ig-rough-edges}

- **Week 1.** The chapter assumes the reader already knows
  what `set.seed()` does; a five-minute board explanation of
  R's random-number generator before Exercise 3 saves
  confusion the chapter does not have room to address.
- **Week 2.** Exercise 2 (placing a published paper on the
  ladder) has no single correct answer; grade it on whether
  the student's reasoning cites a specific determinant from
  the determinant stack in Levels of Reproducibility, not on
  which rung they name.
- **Weeks 5 to 6.** Both labs need Docker. Apple Silicon and
  Windows students will need `--platform linux/amd64`
  (covered in the text) and, on Windows, WSL2; budget a
  studio hour before week 5 for environment setup, since
  this is where a course on this schedule is most often
  lost.
- **Week 10.** The restricted-data half of Exercise 4 has a
  worked exemplar in the chapter's own solution, a
  data-availability statement for a registry extract held
  under a data-use agreement. A reasonable rubric: does the
  plan name a specific de-identification or
  controlled-access route, and does it say what happens if
  the data cannot be shared at all, rather than assuming it
  always can be.

## What is not here {#sec-ig-not-here}

```{r}
#| label: ig-coverage
#| include: false
book_text <- function(f) readLines(file.path('analysis/report', f),
                                   warn = FALSE)
covered <- c(
  'licensing and `CITATION.cff`' = any(grepl(
    '^#+ .*Licensing, CITATION.cff',
    book_text('10-archiving-sharing.qmd'))),
  'a shell primer' = file.exists('analysis/report/shell-primer.qmd'),
  'an HPC section' = any(grepl('^#+ .*HPC',
                               book_text('06-backends-runtimes.qmd'))))
```

This guide does not hold alternate exercises, exam
questions, slide decks, or a second set of solutions. Of
the content gaps the coverage sweep of `REFACTOR-PLAN.md`
section 10.10 found,
`r if (all(covered)) paste0('all have since been filled: ', knitr::combine_words(names(covered)), ' are in the book.') else paste0(knitr::combine_words(names(covered)[covered]), if (sum(covered) == 1) ' is' else ' are', ' now in the book, and ', knitr::combine_words(names(covered)[!covered]), ' remain open.')`
The week table needs no separate row for them: licensing
falls in Chapter 13 (week 10), the HPC worked example in
the optional Chapter 8, and the shell primer is an
appendix to assign with the week 1 setup check.
